adjudication_records.issue_text: In InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin cache-hit path, raw models from session.identityProviders().getById(id) are returned without applying createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel, unlike the isInvalid and idp==null fallback paths, causing inconsistent org-scoped semantics between warm and cold cache

adjudication.rationale: In the new getForLogin implementation, the cache-miss path returns `idpDelegate.getForLogin(...).map(this::createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel)` when `isInvalid(cacheKey)` is true, and the `idp == null` fallback also returns the delegate stream mapped through `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel`. However, on the normal cache-hit path it iterates cached IDs, does `IdentityProviderModel idp = session.identityProviders().getById(id);` and returns `identityProviders.stream()` without wrapping via `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel`, leading to different returned model semantics depending on cache warmth.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getLoginPredicate dereferences idp.getConfig() without a null guard, causing NPE when an IDP has an organizationId set but null config map, turning IDP create/update/remove writes into 500 errors

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` to include `.and(idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)))`. For any IDP with a non-null `organizationId`, the RHS is evaluated; if `idp.getConfig()` is null, this will throw an NPE. The new cache invalidation paths (`registerIDPLoginInvalidation*`) call `getLoginPredicate().test(idp)` during create/update/remove, so such an NPE would surface during those write operations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In the "current search is not yet cached" branch of getForLogin, cache.addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter()) is used while the first-population branch uses startupRevision, so invalidations registered between the delegate fetch and addRevisioned are silently absorbed, allowing stale cached data

adjudication.rationale: In getForLogin, the initial population path stores the IdentityProviderListQuery via cache.addRevisioned(query, startupRevision), but the "current search is not yet cached" path stores it via cache.addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter()). This inconsistency is visible in the diff. If startupRevision is meant to ensure that invalidations occurring during the delegate fetch (between getCurrentRevision()/fetch and addRevisioned) are not masked, then using getCurrentCounter at insertion time can record the entry as "fresh" even if an invalidation happened mid-fetch, allowing stale results to be cached.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.remove, idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) now runs unconditionally on every removal even on the isInvalid path where the result may be unused, adding a permanent DB query cost to the IDP removal write path

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `remove(String alias)` to eagerly load `IdentityProviderModel storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias);` before checking `isInvalid(cacheKey)`. This means a delegate lookup now happens on every removal, whereas previously `idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)` was only invoked on the `isInvalid(cacheKey)` path. The loaded `storedIdp` is then used for `registerIDPInvalidation(storedIdp)` (invalid path) and `registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp)` (always), but this still introduces an unconditional delegate/DB cost that could have been avoided when cache data was sufficient or when the IDP doesn’t qualify for login invalidation. This is a performance concern rather than a correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The getLoginPredicate change in OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean silently redefines which IDPs FetchMode.ALL returns for org-linked, non-brokerPublic IDPs — an IDP linked to an organization without brokerPublic=true is now excluded even under FetchMode.ALL, making org-private identity brokers vanish from the org's login page, with no test coverage or acceptance criterion

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` to require `idp.getOrganizationId() == null || brokerPublic==true` (server-spi change). That predicate is used to decide which IDPs qualify “for login”, so it will now filter out any org-linked IDP that is not `BROKER_PUBLIC`, even when `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean` calls `getForLogin(ALL, orgId)`. This is a behavioral change that can make org-private brokers disappear from the org login page. The added test `testCacheIDPForLogin` only covers org-linked IDPs with `BROKER_PUBLIC=true` and does not cover the org-private case, matching the finding’s “no test coverage” point.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test cleanup in OrganizationCacheTest registers removal against the nonexistent alias 'alias' instead of 'idp-alias-' + i, causing cleanup remove() calls to hit a 404, leaking the 20+ created IDPs and org links into the shared test realm and contaminating subsequent tests

adjudication.rationale: In the new `testCacheIDPForLogin` loop, IDPs are created with aliases `"idp-alias-" + i`, but cleanup is registered as `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);` (literal "alias"). This will not remove the created IDPs during cleanup, so the test can leak created IDPs (and any org links created later) into the shared realm and affect subsequent tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The diff never verifies cache invalidation when a login-eligible IDP is created or removed — the create()/remove() registerIDPLoginInvalidation paths for an IDP satisfying getLoginPredicate are executed zero times, leaving the critical stale-cache prevention unverified

adjudication.rationale: The new caching/invalidation logic for login IDPs is exercised in tests, but the specific invalidation paths on create()/remove() for a login-eligible IDP are not actually verified. In testCacheIDPForLogin(), the only post-cache operations that call create/remove are: creating idp-alias-20 with hideOnLogin=true (explicitly NOT login-eligible) and removing idp-alias-1 (disabled, thus not login-eligible). The initial batch creation includes some login-eligible IDPs, but the login caches are populated only afterwards, so the test never asserts that creating a login-eligible IDP invalidates an already-populated login cache, nor that removing a login-eligible IDP does. This is a concrete test gap for the new registerIDPLoginInvalidation(...) calls in create() and remove().

adjudication_records.issue_text: No verification that getForLogin returns organization-aware models on the cache-hit path — tests only assert cache entry sizes and never check that cache-hit results carry the same createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel wrapping as the delegate path

adjudication.rationale: In `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider#getForLogin`, the cache-miss path explicitly wraps results via `.map(this::createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel)`, but the cache-hit path returns `identityProviders.stream()` built from `session.identityProviders().getById(id)` without an explicit `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel` mapping. The added test `testCacheIDPForLogin` only asserts `IdentityProviderListQuery` presence and ID set sizes (e.g., `getIDPs(orgaId).size()`), and never asserts that returned models on a cache hit are organization-aware/wrapped the same way as the delegate path. This is a concrete gap in coverage for the newly added cache-hit logic, even if it may be correct depending on what `getById` returns.

adjudication_records.issue_text: InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin has no handling or verification for an organization being deleted or an IDP being unlinked from an organization outside the update() path, so cached searchKey sets can keep returning unlinked IDPs on ORG_ONLY/ALL login queries indefinitely

adjudication.rationale: The new getForLogin() cache stores a Set of IDP internalIds keyed by (realm, fetchMode) plus a per-searchKey (organizationId/"") entry in IdentityProviderListQuery, and the cached path simply rehydrates by id (session.identityProviders().getById(id)) without re-checking org linkage or the login predicate. In this diff, invalidation of these login caches is only registered from create(), remove(), and update() (via registerIDPLoginInvalidation*). There is no invalidation shown for changes in org↔IDP linkage or org deletion unless those operations flow through update()/remove(). So the reviewer concern about potentially stale ORG_ONLY/ALL results is diff-grounded as an edge-case/invalidation-coverage gap, but the claim that it will happen “outside the update() path” cannot be verified from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getLoginPredicate in IdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:254 changes the login-visibility contract (excluding org-linked IDPs without BROKER_PUBLIC) for all implementations, bundled into a caching-only PR without a stated requirement — scope drift

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change the global login-visibility predicate in `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` by adding `.and(idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)))`, which will exclude org-linked IDPs unless `BROKER_PUBLIC` is true for all implementations using this predicate. The rest of the PR is primarily adding caching/invalidation for `getForLogin` in `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider` plus related tests, so the concern that this is a broader behavior/contract change bundled with caching work is grounded in the diff (even though whether it’s “unstated” can’t be verified here).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Added idp.isEnabled() re-filter in OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean.java:75,80 is a correctness fix beyond caching scope and changes results for the non-cached path

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add an `idp.isEnabled()` filter in `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean` (lines shown), which will indeed apply regardless of caching. However, nothing in the diff indicates this is incorrect or problematic; the added inline comment explicitly ties it to wrapping behavior (“idp might have been wrapped”), making it plausibly part of ensuring correct results when using the new cached/wrapped `getForLogin` path. The claim that this is an improper “beyond caching scope” change is subjective and not a verifiable defect or review issue from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Login caches are invalidated only on create/update/remove through the Infinispan provider; organization-side mutations (OrganizationProvider, e.g. addIdentityProvider, org deletion) bypass invalidation, leaving getForLogin caches permanently stale

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds getForLogin() caching keyed only by realm+FetchMode (cacheKeyForLogin) and invalidates those caches only from InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider on IDP create/update/remove (registerIDPLoginInvalidation / registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate). Nothing in this diff shows invalidation triggered by organization-side link mutations (e.g., organizations().get(...).identityProviders().addIdentityProvider(...), org deletion). While the added test exercises such a mutation and expects caches cleared, the invalidation mechanism for that path is not visible in this diff, so the finding is a plausible architectural gap but not directly verifiable as a defect here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The test only covers IDP-model updates before linking, masking the pure org-side-linkage path; the invariant 'login cache reflects org membership' is not enforced or tested

adjudication.rationale: In `testCacheIDPForLogin` step (4), the test performs an IDP update (`BROKER_PUBLIC` set) and then links the IDP to an org via `organizations().get(orgaId).identityProviders().addIdentityProvider(...)`, and only then asserts the login caches are cleared. It does not isolate/verify the “pure org-side linkage” path (link/unlink while login caches are populated) causes invalidation by itself. This is relevant because the new invalidation logic added in this diff (`registerIDPLoginInvalidation*`) is only invoked from `create/update/remove` in `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider`, while org membership changes occur through the organization API (not shown here). The test therefore doesn’t directly enforce the invariant that login caches reflect org membership changes independent of an IDP model update.

adjudication_records.issue_text: OrganizationCacheTest.java cleanup registers removal for alias "alias" but created providers use idp-alias-0..20, causing null::remove NPE or leaked IDPs polluting subsequent assertions

adjudication.rationale: In OrganizationCacheTest.testCacheIDPForLogin(), inside the loop creating IDPs with aliases "idp-alias-"+i, the cleanup is registered as `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);` (literal "alias"). That does not match any created provider alias, so `identityProviders().get("alias")` will return null and `null::remove` will NPE when cleanup runs (and/or fail to remove the created IDPs, leaking them into later tests).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Only getForLogin is cached; getByFlow and getByOrganization remain uncached, leaving the hot admin-console path uncached — possibly under-scoped relative to 'cache IDP list queries'

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not show that “only getForLogin is cached.” This provider already contains caching logic for other IDP queries, notably `getByOrganization(...)` (it exists in the same class and uses organization-specific cache keys like `cacheKeyOrgId(...)`, and there is an existing test `testCacheIDPByOrg`). The change adds caching for `getForLogin(...)`, but it does not remove or replace existing caching for other paths. While `getByFlow(...)` still delegates uncached (`return idpDelegate.getByFlow(...)`), the finding’s broader claim that getByOrganization remains uncached and that caching is under-scoped relative to “cache IDP list queries” is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getForLogin cache-hit path returns unwrapped IdentityProviderModels while cache-miss path returns organization-aware wrappers, causing inconsistent behavior between cached and uncached requests

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that the cache-miss path explicitly wraps results via `map(this::createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel)`, while the cache-hit path reconstructs results via `session.identityProviders().getById(id)` and returns them directly. However, from this diff alone we cannot verify that `getById` returns an *unwrapped* `IdentityProviderModel`—it may itself return the organization-aware wrapper (the same pattern already exists in `getByOrganization`, which also uses `getById` on cache hits). Therefore the finding’s claim that cache hits return unwrapped models is not verifiable from the provided changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getLoginPredicate's new organization clause is not reflected in getLoginSearchOptions, so the delegate query returns org-linked non-public IDPs that leak to realm-level login pages

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` was tightened with a new organization/public clause (`idp.getOrganizationId() == null || ...BROKER_PUBLIC`), but `getLoginSearchOptions()` was not updated in this PR (it appears unchanged in the diff). If any `getForLogin(...)` implementation relies on `getLoginSearchOptions()` to push filters down into storage queries (rather than applying `getLoginPredicate()` post-fetch), this creates an inconsistency where query-time filtering may not match the predicate’s semantics. However, the diff alone does not prove the asserted “leak to realm-level login pages” because the `getForLogin` delegate implementation and how it uses search options vs predicate is not shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getLoginPredicate dereferences idp.getConfig() without a null guard, risking NPE during create/update/remove of IDPs with null config maps

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `getLoginPredicate()` now evaluates `Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC))` without checking whether `idp.getConfig()` is null. That is a concrete potential NPE. However, the diff alone does not establish that `IdentityProviderModel#getConfig()` can ever be null in practice (tests use `idpRep.getConfig()` which appears non-null), so the claim that this will occur on create/update/remove cannot be verified solely from this PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Cached getForLogin results are returned as a HashSet with nondeterministic iteration order, unlike the delegate's ordered stream, causing unstable ordering depending on cache warmth

adjudication.rationale: In the new cached path of `getForLogin`, IDs are collected into a `Set` (`collect(Collectors.toSet())`) and then resolved into a `HashSet<IdentityProviderModel>` before returning `identityProviders.stream()`. Both `toSet()` (typically `HashSet`) and the explicit `new HashSet<>()` discard any encounter order, so the cached result stream can have nondeterministic iteration order. However, the diff does not establish that `idpDelegate.getForLogin(...)` is ordered or that ordering is part of the method contract, so it’s a real, diff-grounded determinism concern but not a verifiable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getForLogin cache accumulates one map entry per organizationId forever in a single cache object, causing unbounded growth and write amplification (full realm IDP reload per new organization)

adjudication.rationale: The new caching in `getForLogin` uses a single cache key per realm+`FetchMode` (`cacheKeyForLogin(realm, mode)`), and stores results keyed by `searchKey` inside an `IdentityProviderListQuery` (`String searchKey = organizationId != null ? organizationId : "";` then `query.getIDPs(searchKey)`). When a new `organizationId` is queried and not present (`cached == null`), it rebuilds the cache entry as `new IdentityProviderListQuery(..., searchKey, cached, query)`, which (by construction) implies retaining prior query data while adding a new per-org entry. This can lead to the cached object accumulating one entry per distinct organizationId over time, and each new org query causes an invalidate + rewrite of the whole `IdentityProviderListQuery` object (write amplification). However, the claim of a “full realm IDP reload per new organization” is not directly verifiable from the diff because the delegate call is `idpDelegate.getForLogin(mode, organizationId)` (scoped to that org/mode), not explicitly a full reload.

adjudication_records.issue_text: OrganizationCacheTest registers cleanup against literal alias 'alias' instead of the created idp-alias-N providers, leaking test IDPs into the shared realm

adjudication.rationale: In `OrganizationCacheTest.testCacheIDPForLogin()`, inside the loop creating providers with aliases `idp-alias-0` .. `idp-alias-19`, cleanup is registered as `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);` (literal string "alias"), not the created alias (e.g., `idp-alias-" + i`). This means the created IDPs are not cleaned up, potentially leaking test data into the shared realm and affecting other tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getForLogin semantics silently changed for all storage providers: org-linked IDPs without OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC are now excluded from the login predicate, causing behavior change (org-linked non-public brokers disappearing from login page) in a caching PR with no migration note

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the global login predicate used by `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` to add `idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC))`. This will exclude any org-linked IDP whose `BROKER_PUBLIC` config is absent/false from `getForLogin(...)` results across *all* storage providers (not just the new Infinispan caching implementation), which is a semantic/backwards-compatibility change. Whether intended or not, it’s a scope/behavior change introduced alongside caching work and is not merely an internal cache detail.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Inconsistent cache behavior in InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin: cache-miss path wraps results via createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel but cache-hit path returns unwrapped getById models, so returned object types/behavior differ depending on cache state

adjudication.rationale: In `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin`, the cache-miss path returns `idpDelegate.getForLogin(...).map(this::createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel)`, but the cache-hit path rebuilds results via `session.identityProviders().getById(id)` and returns `identityProviders.stream()` without applying `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel`. This makes returned `IdentityProviderModel` instances differ depending on cache state, matching the reported inconsistency.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Added isEnabled() re-check filters in OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean are compensating patches rather than fixes; other callers of getForLogin remain exposed to wrapped IDPs that fail the login predicate

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean added an extra `idp.isEnabled()` filter with a comment about wrapping, but the finding’s broader claim that this is merely a “compensating patch” and that “other callers of getForLogin remain exposed” is not verifiable from the PR diff. The diff does not show any other callers, nor does it demonstrate that wrapped IDPs returned by `getForLogin` fail the login predicate or include disabled IDPs. `getForLogin` itself is populated from `idpDelegate.getForLogin(...)`, which already applies the login predicate before caching IDs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getLoginPredicate dereferences idp.getConfig() without a null guard, causing NPE for IdentityProviderModels with null config map, potentially making the realm's login page throw a 500 (DoS on authentication)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds to `getLoginPredicate()` a predicate `idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC))`, which dereferences `idp.getConfig()` without a null guard. The diff itself doesn’t show whether `IdentityProviderModel.getConfig()` is guaranteed non-null, so the claimed NPE/DoS is plausible but not verifiable from the PR alone; however, the lack of null-safety is a concrete, diff-grounded robustness issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getForLogin cache key cacheKeyForLogin(realm, mode) is scoped only by realm and fetch mode while containing per-organization result sets keyed by attacker-influenced organizationId, enabling cross-tenant cache interference where one organization's traffic can evict/replace another organization's cached login-IDP set

adjudication.rationale: In getForLogin(), the top-level cache key is cacheKeyForLogin(realm, mode) (realm+mode only), while per-organization results are stored inside an IdentityProviderListQuery keyed by `searchKey` (organizationId or ""). This means one organization’s access pattern can affect the single shared cache entry: if `query.getIDPs(searchKey)` is null for a new orgId, the code calls `cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey)` and rewrites the entry, which can evict/refresh the shared structure and cause cache churn for other orgs. However, the diff does not show a correctness/security data-mixing bug (results are still keyed by orgId within the query), so the “cross-tenant cached set replacement” claim is overstated; it’s primarily a scoping/performance/architecture concern grounded in the shared key and invalidation behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Cleanup in OrganizationCacheTest uses alias "alias" which matches none of the 21 created IDPs, so cleanup removes nothing and brokers plus organization links leak into the shared test realm, causing order-dependent test pollution

adjudication.rationale: In `OrganizationCacheTest.testCacheIDPForLogin`, the loop creates IDPs with aliases `idp-alias-0`..`idp-alias-19`, but registers cleanup as `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);` (same pattern for `idp-alias-20`). Since no IDP with alias literal "alias" is created in this diff, the cleanup removes nothing, leaving created brokers (and later org links) in the shared test realm and causing cross-test pollution/order dependence.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The new test discards the Stream<IdentityProviderModel> returned by getForLogin and asserts only internal IdentityProviderListQuery cache entries, so the public contract of the method is unverified and wrong return values would still pass

adjudication.rationale: In `testCacheIDPForLogin`, calls like `session.identityProviders().getForLogin(FetchMode.REALM_ONLY, null);` are not consumed/collected, and the test assertions focus exclusively on `IdentityProviderListQuery` cache contents (e.g., `assertEquals(5, identityProviderListQuery.getIDPs("").size())`). The test never verifies the actual `Stream<IdentityProviderModel>` results (aliases/enablement/org-awareness), so an incorrect stream return (e.g., wrong filtering/mapping) could still pass as long as the cache entry sizes match.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The second-chance cache-miss branch in getForLogin (query != null && query.getIDPs(searchKey) == null) is never exercised by any test, so the merge path and revision/counter choice ships untested

adjudication.rationale: In `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider#getForLogin`, the branch `query != null` then `cached = query.getIDPs(searchKey); if (cached == null) { ... new IdentityProviderListQuery(..., query); cache.addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter()); }` is only reached when the same `cacheKeyForLogin(realm, mode)` exists but a *new* `searchKey` (different `organizationId`/"" value) is requested. The added test `testCacheIDPForLogin` only ever queries each `FetchMode` with a single `searchKey` (REALM_ONLY with "", ORG_ONLY/ALL with `orgaId`), so it never exercises the `cached == null` “second-chance cache-miss” merge path nor validates the revision/counter selection there.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The stale-cache fallback branch in getForLogin (idp == null inside cached-ID loop leading to registerInvalidation and delegate re-fetch) is never triggered by any test, leaving its correctness unverified

adjudication.rationale: In `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin`, there is an explicit stale-cache fallback when iterating cached internal IDs: if `session.identityProviders().getById(id)` returns `null`, it registers invalidation and re-fetches from the delegate. The newly added `testCacheIDPForLogin` exercises cache population and invalidation on create/update/remove, but it never creates a situation where the cached ID set contains an IDP internalId that later becomes missing while the login cache entry remains present (e.g., removing a login-qualifying IDP without invalidating the login cache). Therefore, the `idp == null` branch’s behavior is not covered by the tests in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The new .filter(idp -> idp.isEnabled()) in OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean has no test; no test asserts a disabled IDP is absent from the rendered login IDP list when served from cache

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new defensive filter in `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean.searchForIdentityProviders(...)`: `.filter(idp -> idp.isEnabled() && !Objects.equals(existingIDP, idp.getAlias()))` (comment says IDP might have been wrapped). The newly added test `testCacheIDPForLogin` exercises `session.identityProviders().getForLogin(...)` caching and counts, but it does not cover the bean’s rendering/search path nor specifically assert that a disabled IDP is excluded at the bean level when results come from cache/wrapped models. So the finding (missing test for this new bean-level behavior) is diff-grounded, but it’s not itself a defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Hardcoded count assertions like assertEquals(5, ...) in OrganizationCacheTest assume TEST_REALM_NAME contains zero pre-existing login-eligible IDPs, making tests vulnerable to order/pollution-dependent off-by-N failures

adjudication.rationale: The newly added `testCacheIDPForLogin()` makes hardcoded size assertions such as `assertEquals(5, identityProviderListQuery.getIDPs("").size())`, `assertEquals(10, ...)`, etc., after creating 20 IDPs. In the diff, the test does not first ensure the realm has no pre-existing login-eligible IDPs (it only adds more), so if `TEST_REALM_NAME` already contains IDPs from realm setup or prior tests, these exact counts could become off-by-N and order/pollution-dependent. This is test fragility rather than a product defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getLoginPredicate in IdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:254 silently reclassifies existing org-linked identity providers from available to unavailable for login on upgrade, with no data migration setting BROKER_PUBLIC and no feature flag to stage the cutover

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` to additionally require `idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC))`. Because `Boolean.parseBoolean(null)` is `false`, any existing organization-linked IDP without `BROKER_PUBLIC=true` will no longer satisfy the login predicate (i.e., it will stop appearing in `getForLogin(...)`). The diff does not show any migration/defaulting logic or staging mechanism for existing data, so the compatibility/upgrade concern is real and diff-grounded, even if the behavior change might be intended.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Invalidation gating in InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.registerIDPLoginInvalidation* allows mixed old/new pods during rolling deploy to serve contradictory login lists because caches populated under the old predicate remain valid under the new diff-comparison logic

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the effective login-eligibility predicate (IdentityProviderStorageProvider.LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate now additionally filters by organization/public config), but the distributed cache key for login lists (InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.cacheKeyForLogin) is unchanged and contains no versioning/salt tied to predicate semantics. As a result, a login-list cache entry populated by older code could be reused by newer code without invalidation (especially if no IDP updates occur), leading to inconsistent results across nodes during a rolling deploy. The invalidation gating in registerIDPLoginInvalidation* relies on the (new) predicate to decide whether to invalidate and won’t inherently flush preexisting entries created under the old predicate.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Login cache invalidation in registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate is gated on update() being called through IdentityProviderStorageProvider, so org-IDP link mutations via other paths (e.g., OrganizationProvider.removeIdentityProvider, org deletion cascades) leave IdentityProviderListQuery entries stale

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, login-cache invalidation is wired only into IDP lifecycle methods on InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider: create() calls registerIDPLoginInvalidation(model), update() calls registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate(original, updated), and remove() calls registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp). There is no diff evidence of invalidation being triggered when an IDP’s organization linkage changes via non-IDP update paths (e.g., organization->identityProviders().add/remove or org deletion cascades). Since getForLogin() now caches results under cacheKeyForLogin(realm, mode) and varies by organizationId inside the cached IdentityProviderListQuery, missing invalidation on org-link mutations would be a concrete staleness risk, but the diff alone doesn’t show whether other components (e.g., organization provider) also invalidate these login keys.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The unlink/invalidation path is untested — the test only exercises the add path via addIdentityProvider

adjudication.rationale: The new test `testCacheIDPForLogin` exercises caching and invalidation on IDP create/update/remove and on linking an IDP to an org via `testRealm().organizations().get(orgaId).identityProviders().addIdentityProvider(...)` (step 4). However, it never exercises the opposite operation (unlink/removal of an IDP from an organization) to verify that the `getForLogin` caches keyed by `cacheKeyForLogin(realm, mode)` are invalidated/updated correctly when an org link is removed. Given the new login-cache behavior and invalidation logic added in `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider`, this is a specific untested edge-path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Cached getForLogin path returns raw models via getById while delegate-fallback paths return organization-aware wrapped models via createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel, causing cache-hit/miss behavior divergence

adjudication.rationale: In the new `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider#getForLogin`, the cache-miss path returns `idpDelegate.getForLogin(...).map(this::createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel)`, and the null-IDP fallback also maps `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel`. But on a cache hit it rebuilds results via `session.identityProviders().getById(id)` and returns `identityProviders.stream()` without applying `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel`, so cache-hit vs cache-miss can return different `IdentityProviderModel` types/behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getForLogin searchKey-miss branch adds revisioned query with getCurrentCounter() instead of startupRevision, defeating the stale-entry guard and allowing stale internal IDs to be served until next invalidation

adjudication.rationale: In `getForLogin`, the searchKey-miss branch explicitly invalidates the cache key (`cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey)`), reloads IDs from the delegate, and then stores a new `IdentityProviderListQuery` via `cache.addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter())`. The finding’s claim that using `getCurrentCounter()` (vs `startupRevision`) “defeats the stale-entry guard” and “allows stale internal IDs to be served” is not verifiable from this diff: the diff does not show how `addRevisioned`/revisions are used to guard staleness, nor that `startupRevision` is required here. The behavior could be intentional (storing the refreshed entry at the current counter after invalidation).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Single cache object per FetchMode means each new organizationId evicts previously cached org results, causing full delegate scans and cache churn for multi-org realms

adjudication.rationale: The cache key for getForLogin is per-realm+FetchMode (cacheKeyForLogin), but the cached value is an IdentityProviderListQuery that is explicitly keyed by a per-search "searchKey" (organizationId or ""). When a new organizationId is queried and not yet cached, the code rebuilds the IdentityProviderListQuery using the previous query (new IdentityProviderListQuery(..., searchKey, cached, query)), which indicates prior org results are intended to be retained rather than evicted. The finding’s claim that each new organizationId evicts previously cached org results is not supported by what’s shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Cache-hit path hydrates via getById(id) without the organization-aware wrapper while delegate branches use createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel, producing structurally inconsistent IdentityProviderModels between cached and uncached responses

adjudication.rationale: In the new `getForLogin` implementation, the uncached/invalid path explicitly wraps delegate results via `.map(this::createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel)`, but the cache-hit path reconstructs results by calling `session.identityProviders().getById(id)` and returns them directly without applying `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel` in this method. The diff alone doesn’t show what `getById` returns (it may already wrap), so the claimed inconsistent model structure isn’t fully verifiable here, but the asymmetry in this method is real and worth addressing/confirming.
